specification.outcome: A user can create an ordinary Backlog task or replace an existing Backlog task's canonical specification through normal conversation, without a campaign and without implicitly beginning work.

scenarios.name: create an ordinary backlog task atomically
given: create-task contains title and description accepted by existing semantic parsers and an optional value accepted by parseTaskSpecification
the verified signed board is writable
when: the host evaluates the normal-language request
then: it journals a host-generated operation ID, canonical request digest, task ID, event ID, and observed board head before effects
one signed task-created-from-request event atomically projects metadata plus an Option specification and digest
success reports task ID, event ID, resulting board head, specification digest Option, and published disposition while leaving the task unclaimed in Backlog without campaign provenance

scenarios.name: amend only an existing backlog specification
given: specify-task contains an exact TaskId UUID and a replacement accepted by parseTaskSpecification
the target exists unclaimed in Backlog
the host binds the verified board head and current Option specification digest
then: one task-specified event replaces only specification and digest
identity, title, description, Backlog state, unclaimed state, ordering, priority, and campaign provenance are preserved
no readiness, claim, run, campaign, or worktree effect occurs

scenarios.name: return an idempotent no-op for an unchanged specification
given: the replacement canonical digest equals the current specification digest
then: no event or Git commit is published
TIBER_TASK_SPECIFICATION_UNCHANGED reports task ID, current board head, unchanged disposition, none event ID, and current digest

scenarios.name: reject invalid create requests in deterministic order
given: one or more create-task preconditions are invalid
when: the host evaluates available facts and stops at the first failure
then: precedence is TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_INVALID for malformed shape or a partial specification object, TIBER_SPECIFICATION_INVALID for a complete-shape semantically invalid specification, TIBER_TASK_BOARD_READ_ONLY, TIBER_TASK_ID_COLLISION, TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_UNAUTHORIZED, then TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT
no partial task, specification, campaign, readiness, claim, run, or worktree state is observable

scenarios.name: reject invalid amendment lifecycle before effects
given: the exact target is claimed, is Ready, In Progress, or Done, or changes from unclaimed Backlog to either condition before publication
when: specify-task is evaluated or publication is revalidated after head advancement
then: TIBER_TASK_LIFECYCLE_INVALID is returned before signing or publication
the specification and every preserved task field remain unchanged

scenarios.name: reject other invalid amendments in deterministic order
given: one or more non-lifecycle specify-task preconditions are invalid
when: the host evaluates available facts and stops at the first failure
then: precedence is TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_ID_INVALID for non-UUID or ambiguous resolution, TIBER_SPECIFICATION_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_BOARD_READ_ONLY, TIBER_TASK_NOT_FOUND, TIBER_TASK_LIFECYCLE_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_UNAUTHORIZED, then TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT
no effect occurs and signer failure cannot be mistaken for a retryable race

scenarios.name: handle identifier collision deterministically
given: the host has not yet journaled a create intent
when: a generated task ID or event ID already exists in verified authority
then: it regenerates the task ID and event ID together for at most three total candidate pairs
the first collision-free pair is journaled and remains stable through every later retry
three colliding pairs return TIBER_TASK_ID_COLLISION without publication

scenarios.name: handle concurrent heads without duplicating authority
given: the host journaled stable operation, task, and event IDs plus request digest and observed head
then: an unrelated advance retries with the same IDs only if the task ID, event ID, and operation ID remain absent and every bound target precondition is unchanged
an existing exact operation ID, request digest, IDs, and canonical content is reconciled as prior success
any event-ID, task-ID, operation-ID, request-digest, specification, or lifecycle mismatch returns TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT and never retries into duplicate authority

scenarios.name: reconcile a lost publication receipt
given: publication succeeded but the local receipt was lost
when: the journaled operation resumes after restart
then: exact event operation ID, request digest, task ID, event ID, and canonical content yield the original success fields with reconciled disposition
matching authority is not republished
any mismatch returns TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT

scenarios.name: route ordinary language independently of campaigns
given: the user asks to create a ticket or replace a Backlog specification
no campaign exists or an unrelated campaign is active
then: the closed request is create-task or specify-task rather than campaign-goal or begin-task
campaign state is neither required nor changed and no readiness review or claim begins

acceptanceCriteria: task-created-from-request is one closed signed event containing operation ID, canonical request digest, metadata, and Option specification plus matching Option digest; foldTaskEvents installs the complete task atomically or rejects it.

create-task omitted specification means Option none. A partial object is malformed request shape; a complete-shape value failing semantic parsing is TIBER_SPECIFICATION_INVALID and never degrades to unspecified.

Canonical semantic request payloads are create {kind,title,description,specification Option} and specify {kind,exact resolved taskId,specification}. requestDigest is sha256: plus lowercase SHA-256 of JSON.stringify of that host-canonical payload; conversational wording and generated IDs are excluded.
A separately generated operationId distinguishes a deliberate repeated user request from recovery. Intent and authority events bind operationId, requestDigest, generated IDs, and canonical content.
Specification digest remains digestTaskSpecification: sha256 of JSON.stringify of the parsed canonical specification. Absence is Option {kind:none}, never a sentinel hash.
Generated task/event IDs are paired, bounded to three pre-intent candidates, and stable after journaling.
Safe retry is limited to unrelated head advancement with absent generated identities and unchanged target preconditions. Claimed/state/specification changes require renewed user evaluation.

Success receipts contain code, published|unchanged|reconciled disposition, taskId, full resulting boardHead, specificationDigest Option, and eventId Option. Denials contain stable code and safe operation/task context.
Ordinary operations never promote, prioritize, review, claim, start, create campaign provenance, or alter campaign checkpoints.
exclusions: Changing title or description after creation
Automatically starting, reviewing, ranking, or claiming tasks
Changing campaign scheduling or goal semantics
Weakening signature, ancestry, or lifecycle verification
dependencies: src/core/tasks/task-values.ts semantic metadata, event, operation, and identity parsers
src/core/tasks/readiness.ts canonical specification parser and digest
src/core/tasks/task-board.ts signed event schema, duplicate-authority checks, lifecycle invariants, ordering, priority, and projection
src/adapters/tasks/git-task-remote.ts signer, verified-head observation, operation reconciliation, and fast-forward publisher
src/extension/workflow-request-tool.ts deterministic dispatcher and durable operation journal
specification.architectureImplications: Extend the closed workflow request algebra and host dispatcher with create-task and specify-task. Add one atomic task-created-from-request event and durable operation intent/receipt journal. The host owns parse-once canonicalization, bounded identifier generation, expected-head and expected-digest preconditions, signing, fast-forward publication, conflict classification, and idempotent reconciliation. Inference supplies semantic intent but cannot authorize, retry across changed target state, or trigger readiness/work effects.
